title: Jack Frost
about: A dad who missed too much of his son's life comes back as a snowman for one last Christmas.
cue: Serve the snacks when the snowman comes to life.
faces: Serve the snacks when the snowman comes to life.
Dad came back as a snowman. He can't drink hot chocolate, so I'm having his mug too.

    StartersSnow day toastie fingers with tomato soupCrisp cheese toasties cut in fingers, with homemade tomato soupHow to make it1 onion, diced1 tbsp olive oil2 tins of crushed tomatoes (400g each)300ml chicken stock1 tsp sugar50ml thickened cream8 slices of white bread1 jar Dijon mustard150g leg ham150g cheddar, grated40g butter, softFry the onion in the oil until soft.Add the tomatoes, stock and sugar and simmer, then blitz smooth and stir in the cream.Spread the bread with mustard and make sandwiches with ham and cheddar. Butter the outsides.Fry until golden on both sides.Cut into fingers and serve with cups of soup.Rinkside pretzel bun hot dogsGrilled franks in pretzel buns with slow-fried onions and mustardHow to make it2 onions, sliced20g butter8 frankfurts8 pretzel buns or soft rolls1 bottle American mustard8 dill pickle slices80g cheddar, gratedSlowly fry the onions in the butter until golden.Simmer the frankfurts in water, then grill briefly for colour.Warm the buns in the oven.Split the buns, add a frankfurt to each and top with onions, mustard, pickles and cheddar.MainsFrost family roast beef and YorkshiresMustard rosemary roast beef, roast potatoes, Yorkshire puddings and gravyHow to make it1.5kg beef topside1 tbsp Dijon mustard1 sprig rosemary, chopped1.2kg potatoes, parboiled4 tbsp vegetable oil2 eggs110g plain flour150ml full cream milk400ml beef stock4 carrots1 tbsp honeyRub the beef with the mustard, rosemary and salt. Parboil the potatoes and toss in oil.Roast the beef at 200°C for medium rare, with the potatoes and honey-tossed carrots on another tray.Rest the beef and turn the oven to 220°C. Whisk the eggs, flour and milk into a batter.Heat a little oil in each hole of a muffin tin, pour in the batter and bake without opening the oven.Make gravy from the juices with a spoon of the flour and the stock.Snow day maple roast carrots and sproutsMaple, butter and thyme. Jack's nose is cork, not a carrot.How to make it500g carrots, cut in batons400g brussels sprouts, halved2 tbsp olive oil2 tbsp maple syrup30g butter4 sprigs of thymeCut the carrots and halve the sprouts.Toss with the oil and salt and roast at 220°C until browned at the edges.Melt the butter with the maple syrup and thyme leaves, pour over the hot vegetables and roast until glazed.SweetsSnowman coconut cupcakesVanilla cupcakes rolled in coconut. No, much more.How to make it275g butter, soft150g caster sugar2 eggs200g self-raising flour120ml full cream milk300g icing sugar1 tsp vanilla extract80g desiccated coconut1 tbsp chocolate chips12 small orange lolliesBeat some of the butter with the sugar, add the eggs, then fold in the flour and milk.Divide into cupcake cases and bake at 180°C.Cool completely.Beat the remaining butter with the icing sugar and vanilla until fluffy and white.Dome onto each cupcake and roll in coconut. Press in chocolate chips for eyes and a lolly for a nose.DrinksHarmonica night white hot chocolateHot white chocolate with cinnamon, whipped cream and coconutHow to make it1 L full cream milk1 cinnamon stick150g white chocolate, chopped1 tsp vanilla extract150ml thickened cream, whipped2 tbsp desiccated coconutHeat the milk with the cinnamon until steaming.Remove the cinnamon and whisk in the white chocolate and vanilla until smooth and frothy.Pour into mugs, top with whipped cream and sprinkle with coconut like fresh snow.Cherry cola floatHot enough to melt a snowman, says the radio.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
